purpose: Profile-first warm indexing hotspot attachment on a smaller corpus than the two-project umbrella, before proposing another optimization.

scope.why_not_two_project: Two-project warm wall is ~12–15s plus samply overhead; one-server warm wall is ~10.7s and still exercises JRuby, gems, Java catalog, fact collection, and resolve.
scope.why_not_built_in_sample: Built-in sample indexes in ~0.6s / 39 files and does not represent production hotspots.

cpu_profile_findings.note: Inclusive percentages use samply known_addresses exact RVA resolution. Sample-containment is more reliable than single leaf frames for Rayon-heavy indexing; ModuleNode::body appearing near-ubiquitous is Prism visitation context, not a standalone optimization target.

ranked_spaces.space: project fact collection / Prism visitation under JRuby call-host
ranked_spaces.evidence: phase project ~5.3s (~half of wall); stacks contain JrubyImportProvider ~18%; collect_direct_facts / FactCollector / process_call_node appear together on the project path

ranked_spaces.space: dependency bind + warm gem product wait after project
ranked_spaces.evidence: phase dependencies ~3.7s; gem wait+producer ~0.9s and binding insertion ~0.8s on already-warm persistent hits
ranked_spaces.not: cold gem decode (0 persistent misses on this run)

ranked_spaces.evidence: phase runtime ~2.5s; process-local Java 179 lookups / 11 hits / ~0.76s producer wall
ranked_spaces.caution: persistent Java hits exist across processes; this run still paid local producer cost

ranked_spaces.evidence: phase resolve ~1.5s; method_candidates ~1.4s; samply containment of resolve ~0.03% suggests it is less CPU-dominant than timers imply or is concentrated/short
ranked_spaces.status: already hit-dominated; cache-hit fast path rejected 2026-08-01

decision: No code change yet. Next change must attach to rank-1 (project/JRuby fact-collection call path) or a measured sub-hotspot inside it after a tighter flame inspection, not another dependency-overlap experiment.
